text: CEO, Google Cloud The front door to AI in the workplace Every healthcare organization is working to deliver great care to more people at a lower cost. However, a general AI model is not enough to solve this challenge. Today, healthcare runs on fragmented data. Patient records, coverage policies, and clinical evidence remain trapped across disconnected records, claims systems, and administrative tools that don’t work together. Clinicians are forced to spend nearly 28 hours a week on manually reconciling information, and patients wait for answers about their care and their coverage. Healthcare organizations need a single, secure, governed orchestration layer that coordinates work across the systems they already run, assembling verifiable evidence and taking multi-step workflows through to completion with human oversight. Today, we are announcing Gemini for healthcare . This purpose-built industry solution extends the universal Gemini agent , we introduced last month at Gemini at Work. The Gemini agent is a single, always-on agent for work where employees delegate an objective, and the agent plans the steps, retains organizational context, and routes across the best models to deliver finished outcomes inside the tools teams already use. The Gemini agent is built with enterprise-grade identity administration, fine-grained access control, and centralized policy management directly into its runtime. Every agent operates with a distinct identity, inherits each user’s existing role-based permissions, and enforces strict need-to-know boundaries across every user, sub-agent, and workflow . Working across clinical, financial, and administrative systems, it orchestrates multi-step tasks without forcing teams to switch applications: For providers: Gemini provides a patient’s history across care settings, charts are prepared before the visit, and authorization packets are assembled against payer policy before submission, so fewer claims come back denied. For health plans and payers: Gemini ensures requests are checked against medical policy and organized for the clinical reviewer, and benefits and costs are explained to members from their own plan documents. Gemini for healthcare is built to support HIPAA compliance, with governance running underneath it all. It’s available starting today in preview. Gemini for healthcare empowers payers and providers to orchestrate complex clinical, operational, and administrative workflows. Four components of Gemini for healthcare Developed alongside clinical and health plan leaders, Gemini for healthcare provides an integrated, fully governed environment configured for payers and providers with four core components: Skills for healthcare work: Skills are reusable instructions and context, written by domain experts, that teach Gemini to run a specific task. Purpose-built, multi-step instructions guide the Gemini agent through essential clinical and administrative tasks, such as medical records synthesis, pre-appointment preparation, coverage and policy review, and payer benefit determination. Each skill applies your organization’s policies and plan rules, and teams can build custom skills tailored to the workflows and standard operating procedures unique to their organization. Connectors to clinical, financial, and operational systems: A library of connectors links Gemini directly to the EHR, claims, care management, and administrative systems organizations already run. Gemini queries each system while strictly preserving existing identity and role-based access controls, so teams get unified context without migrating sensitive data or altering permissions. An open healthcare partner ecosystem: Every health system and health plan runs a different mix of systems. Healthcare systems integrators and digital health partners help organizations extend Gemini with specialized solutions, connect it to what they already run, and scale it without lock-in. A secure, governed platform with open model choice: Clinical, security, and IT leaders get one place to set and enforce policies that govern every agent interaction. It is built to support HIPAA compliance, with enterprise-grade access controls, end-to-end audit logging, and verifiable citations so reviewers can check where each answer came from. Because the agent supports model choice, organizations can pair frontier models from Google and leading partners for complex clinical reasoning with fast, cost-efficient models for routine administrative steps under the same governance. Gemini for healthcare takes on the heavy assembly and administrative work that slows down clinical decisions and coverage determinations. At the point of care: Building a longitudinal timeline from fragmented sources: Synthesizes EHR and external records, separates active problems from resolved ones, lists allergies, and flags medication discrepancies. Clinicians get a grounded and unified patient picture in minutes rather than piecing together history across disconnected systems. Reclaiming preparation time between patients: Prepares the patient chart ahead of a scheduled visit or procedure, flagging interval events, current medications, and outstanding clearances, labs, or consents, so care teams walk in with the full picture. Streamlining clinical authorization and appeals: Extracts relevant chart evidence into an audit-ready packet for review, aligned with payer policy, flagging documentation gaps before submission rather than after a denial. If denials do occur, and the record supports it, it drafts an appeal grounded directly in the clinical record and the plan’s policy. At the point of coverage: Accelerating payer review: Checks incoming requests against the health plan’s medical policies and organizes the findings for reviewers, with findings traceable to the submitted documentation and coverage policy. Clinical reviewers spend less time assembling files and more time applying professional judgment. Demystifying benefits and patient financial liability: Parses complex plan benefit booklets to estimate out-of-pocket costs, track deductibles, and verify in-network status, giving member services staff a step-by-step breakdown grounded in the member’s actual plan documents. For Medicare Advantage members, it applies Medicare’s coverage criteria where a plan’s internal rule is stricter. Gemini for healthcare connects directly to core clinical, operational, and industry systems via secure connectors , inheriting each source system’s existing role-based access controls and data permissions. EHRs and clinical data integration: Eligibility, claims, and pricing: Terminology and coding: Coverage and provider reference: Evidence based guidelines: Clinical and operational workflows: Enterprise productivity and collaboration: Security and compliance: Cyera Dataport : Integrates with Cyera for data and agent security, delivering protected health information (PHI) context to support HIPAA audits and compliance reporting. Through our open platform, organizations can deploy specialized partner agents such as ASCO Oncology Guideline Assistant or work with healthcare systems integrators, including 66degrees, Accenture, Altimetrik, AuxoAI, Cognizant, Deloitte, Egen, HCLTech, KPMG, NTT DATA, PwC, Quantiphi, Slalom, Tata Consultancy Services, TEKsystems Global Services, and Wipro, to customize, integrate, and scale these capabilities across complex enterprise architectures without vendor lock-in. When payers and providers can connect data, insights and workflows more seamlessly, we can remove unnecessary complexity, improve performance and help the entire system work better .” — Sandeep Dadlani, Chief Executive Officer, Optum Insight . “Gemini for healthcare serves as a foundation for our unified architecture of reusable AI agents, enabling us to deliver new capabilities and productivity gains significantly faster than traditional development cycles. Our focus going forward is an agentic-AI model, where an intelligence layer drives deeper automation and operational transformation. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts is working toward that future in healthcare with Google Cloud." — Prem Somasundaram, Chief Information Officer, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts. Accelerating clinical research and evidence-based guidelines “For oncology care providers, quick access to current and relevant information is not a luxury, but a necessity. We are excited about what Gemini for healthcare could do to help care providers quickly find the critical information they need, when they need it, so they can drive better outcomes for patients.” — Clifford Hudis, MD, FACP, FASCO, Chief Executive Officer, American Society of Clinical Oncology. Google is both a frontier AI lab and an enterprise cloud. Gemini for healthcare runs on Google Cloud’s secure infrastructure and is built to support HIPAA compliance . Clinical data, prompts, and generated outputs remain within your organization’s governed environment and are never used to train or fine-tune Google’s foundation models. Outputs are grounded in clinical records, plan policies, and your organization’s approved guidelines and evidence, with traceable citations and audit logging that give clinical, compliance, and IT leaders visibility and control. And because we operate the full stack, from infrastructure and models through security and the application layer, we can optimize performance, reliability, and cost together, routing high-volume administrative tasks to fast, low-cost models and reserving high-reasoning models for complex clinical and operational analysis, so organizations can scale AI across the enterprise without scaling spend at the same rate. The launch of Gemini for healthcare marks another step in our commitment to bring the best of Gemini to every professional and every workflow, natively tailored to the way their industry works. Gemini for healthcare is available in preview in the U.S. today, joining our expanding suite of purpose-built solutions for legal , financial services , and government services . We invite leaders across health systems, medical groups, health plan providers, and payers to explore how Gemini can transform their most critical clinical and operational workflows.
